text: The delegation-of-authority limit is a governed data row with a version, read for the caller's role from the authority matrix through rwb-decision. The step compares the chosen route with that limit, records the limit applied and its version in the decision record, and asserts no boundary: the limit value, its boundaries and the matrix row stay open as CG-B2-S1-008-1 until their owner publishes them, and the contract declares the element with its source and no value.
why: The legacy story and FSD S1 A2.8.1 require the approval to be inside the delegated limit, BR-S1-008 forbids writing a business value in code, and no read source publishes the limit, its boundaries, the matrix row or the rule id of the step.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-008 story and depends-on row; FSD S1 A2.8.1, A2.8.3.1 BR-S1-008 and A2.8.3.3; TSD S1 T3.2 and T-A.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-14 and R-UNI-15; Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-04 and DP-06 context
confirm: Owner of rwb-decision with the owner of the authority matrix and the business owner of module S1, before the wave 3 contract tag
impact: If the limit is carried as a rule parameter rather than a reference-data row, the read row and the record element keep their shape and only the owner's answer changes; the approval behaviour is unchanged

text: The four consumed rows are read on the operation each owner publishes, and until that name is published the clients are built against the documented use and their fakes. rwb-case answers the case state and the case move, rwb-decision answers the rule in force, the authority-matrix limit and the decision-log record, and rwb-access answers the authorise check; each is one hop with a 2 s budget and no chain.
why: No source publishes the operation names of the consumed rows, and the plan rows of both stories carry no class C dependency, so the stories must be buildable on Day 1 against a documented use and a fake.
read: Context pack S1 ownership rows; TSD S1 T-A.1, T5.1 and T5.2; FSD S1 A2.8.2 integration points; Template and Rules §R5.4 and §R5.5 DP-11
confirm: Owners of rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-access at the wave 3 tag
impact: A published name is an additive minor version of the baseline and a client change; the case states, the limit element and the record are unchanged

text: The approval element set is carried flat inside Approval: the chosen route, the expected return, the reasons, the confidence, the alternatives, the override reason, the limit applied with its version, the rule id and the rule version. The recommendation of FEAT-VAL-05 to FEAT-VAL-07 is read from the workflow state and echoed in that answer; it adds no operation, no second assessment and no REST row. Where a type, a nullability or an element name is not published, the baseline carries the placeholder and an open P3 item.
why: TSD S1 T-A.2 names RouteRequest and Approval without a field table, FSD S1 A2.7 and A2.8 give no message element, and the recommendation is computed inside the same workflow, so no surface exists to publish it as a separate contract.
read: TSD S1 T-A.2; FSD S1 A2.7.2 and A2.8.3.2; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-VAL-07 and FEAT-VAL-08; FSD S1 requirements REQ-S1-005 and REQ-S1-006
confirm: Platform API owner and solution architect, S1, at the v1 freeze
impact: A refused nesting or type is a breaking change before the first consumer pins v1; after publication it is a major version 2

text: No S1 rule package is in force for the approval. The step reads whatever rule id and rule version the rwb-decision answer carries for the business date, records them with the limit applied, and applies no local decision table of its own; if the answer carries no rule id, the record carries the placeholder and the version of the decision answer, never an invented rule id.
why: Both legacy criteria require the result to be recorded with the rule version, and no source publishes an S1 approval rule, its parameter or its row.
read: FSD S1 A2.8.3.1 BR-S1-008 and A2.8.4.1; TSD S1 T3.2 and T8; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 Rules sheet; Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-04 context
confirm: Owner of rwb-decision with the business owner of module S1 before the S1 package is promoted
impact: A published rule id and version fill the same element with no behavioural change; a rule parameter would move the limit read to the rule answer and keep the record shape

why: The overlay for D-RCV-60 records a missing approval or status as an assumption and continues at Draft rather than stopping the run.
